unit.can_do_en: say who is in my family.

judge.reason: Both ask 'Do you have children?' Only register differs.
Both say 'Yes, I have two children.' Spoken kaks equals kaksi.
Both ask how old they are. Spoken ne means they, same as he; the number and subject are unchanged.

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.text_puhe: Poika on viis ja tyttö kaheksan.
lines.text_kirja: Poika on viisi ja tyttö kahdeksan.
lines.gloss_en: My son is five and my daughter eight.

judge.reason: Boy is five and girl eight in both. Only the spoken forms of the numbers differ.

lines.speaker: Ville
lines.text_puhe: Kiva ikä! Mul on yks tytär. Se on kolme.
lines.text_kirja: Kiva ikä! Minulla on yksi tytär. Hän on kolme.
lines.gloss_en: Nice age! I have one daughter. She's three.

judge.reason: Both say 'I have one daughter. She is three.' Spoken se equals hän.
Both ask 'What is her name?' Spoken sen nimi equals hänen nimensä.

lines.speaker: Ville
lines.text_puhe: Ella. Se puhuu jo tosi paljon!
lines.text_kirja: Ella. Hän puhuu jo todella paljon!
lines.gloss_en: Ella. She already talks a lot!

judge.reason: Both say the girl is called Ella and already talks a lot. Spoken tosi equals todella.
Both mean 'My children too.' Spoken kans equals myös.

forms.why_en: Means 'is...?'. The question ending -ko turns 'on' (is) into a question.
Sinä with -lla. With on it means 'you have'. Speech shortens it to sul.
Lapsi becomes lapsia in a question about having any. Speech turns the last a into i: lapsii.

After a number like kaksi, the word takes -a: lapsi becomes lasta, 'two children'.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.

forms.form_name_en: nominative singular, with the possessive ending for his, her or their
forms.why_en: Books add -nsä for 'his, her or their': nimensä. Speech drops it and says sen nimi.
Puhua doubles its last vowel for he or she: puhuu.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.

forms.form_name_en: nominative plural, with the possessive ending for my
forms.why_en: lapsi, child. -set makes many, -ni adds 'my': lapseni. Speech says mun lapset and drops -ni.
